caption: Name, e-mail, and phone are STRING; birthday is DATE — the policy's RETURNS type must match the column.

code:
CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY governance.tasty_pii_string_mask
AS (val STRING) RETURNS STRING ->
CASE
  WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('ACCOUNTADMIN','SYSADMIN')
    THEN val
  WHEN SYSTEM$GET_TAG_ON_CURRENT_COLUMN('TAGS.TASTY_PII') = 'PHONE_NUMBER'
    THEN CONCAT(LEFT(val,3), '-***-****')
  WHEN SYSTEM$GET_TAG_ON_CURRENT_COLUMN('TAGS.TASTY_PII') = 'EMAIL'
    THEN CONCAT('**~MASKED~**','@', SPLIT_PART(val, '@', -1))
  ELSE '**~MASKED~**'
END;

CREATE OR REPLACE MASKING POLICY governance.tasty_pii_date_mask
AS (val DATE) RETURNS DATE ->
CASE
  WHEN CURRENT_ROLE() IN ('ACCOUNTADMIN','SYSADMIN')
    THEN val
  WHEN SYSTEM$GET_TAG_ON_CURRENT_COLUMN('TAGS.TASTY_PII') = 'BIRTHDAY'
    THEN DATE_FROM_PARTS(YEAR(val) - (YEAR(val) % 5), 1, 1)
  ELSE NULL
END;
caption: Privileged roles exit first; everyone else falls through to a tag-driven CASE branch.
BIRTHDAY_DATE bucketed to the 1st of a 5-year window — DATE_FROM_PARTS at work.
SHOW / DESCRIBE to inspect; SET / UNSET on ALTER TABLE ... MODIFY COLUMN to attach or remove.
How a policy got attached is invisible at query time; only the masking behavior shows.
